title: Safer Schools Reaches 12,000 Students Across Abuja FCT
author: RAP Initiative
excerpt: Our Safer Schools programme completed its latest round of workshops across 18 schools in the FCT, equipping thousands of students with life-saving road safety knowledge.
paragraphs: In the third quarter of 2025, RAP Initiative's Safer Schools team visited 18 primary and secondary schools across the FCT — from Garki to Gwagwalada — delivering structured road safety curricula to 12,000 students.

The workshops covered pedestrian safety, why seatbelts save lives, the dangers of distracted driving, and how to respond in an emergency. Each school received a road safety kit: teaching guides, posters, and a pledge card for students to take home.
"The children were so engaged," said lead facilitator Amaka Nwosu. "They asked questions about the roads near their homes, they worried about their parents. It showed us this work matters deeply."

Following each workshop, class teachers received a follow-up guide to embed road safety into regular lessons — a strategy that our 2024 survey found leads to 92% retention of core safety messages three months later.
The next cohort of schools begins in October. If your school would like to take part, contact us at hello@rapinitiative.org.

title: Inside Safer Drivers: 200 Danfo Operators Complete Training
author: RAP Initiative
excerpt: A look at our latest driver training cohort in Lagos — what they learned, what changed, and what the road looks like from the other side of the wheel.
paragraphs: Two hundred danfo operators completed the Safer Drivers programme at Ojota Motor Park in July 2025 — the largest single cohort in RAP Initiative's history.

Over three days, drivers worked through modules on defensive driving, alcohol and fatigue awareness, vehicle pre-trip checks, and how to respond when a passenger is in distress. The sessions were led in Yoruba and Pidgin to ensure full comprehension.
"We drive these roads every day," said one participant, Biodun Adeyemi. "Now I understand what I'm actually risking — for my passengers and for myself. I'll drive differently."

The training was delivered in partnership with the Lagos State Bus Operators' Association, which agreed to make the certification a condition for renewal of stage permits — a significant policy win that will create lasting change.
RAP Initiative plans to run two more cohorts before year-end, targeting Oshodi and Ikorodu motor parks.

title: RAP Initiative Briefs FRSC on Black-Spot Findings from Eyes on the Road
author: RAP Initiative
excerpt: Our community road audit data — 180 black spots mapped across 9 LGAs — was presented to FRSC leadership and FCT state legislators in Abuja.
paragraphs: On 30 June 2025, RAP Initiative's Voices on the Road team presented findings from the Eyes on the Road community audit programme to senior FRSC officials and members of the FCT House of Representatives Road Safety Committee.

The briefing covered 180 black spots — dangerous road sections identified by community monitors through our citizen reporting platform — spanning 9 LGAs. The data included crash frequency, contributing factors such as poor lighting, missing speed signs, and unmaintained road surfaces, along with community-recommended interventions.

FRSC Corps Commander Adamu Usman welcomed the data, noting that community-led intelligence fills a critical gap in official records. Three of the reported corridors are now under active review for safety improvement works.
"This is what advocacy looks like," said RAP Initiative Head of Campaigns, Hauwa Umaru. "We don't just raise awareness — we put evidence in the hands of people who can change the roads."
The full briefing document is available to partner organisations and government agencies on request. Contact partners@rapinitiative.org.
